Luca (CS Ops): Quick weekly check-in for AcmeCorp — error mix looks different this week, wanted to surface the breakdown and top endpoints so we can prioritize follow-ups.
Ava (CSE): thanks — do you have raw counts or just percentages?
Luca (CS Ops): raw + pct. Short summary: 5xx = 42% (mainly 502s), timeouts = 34% (client-side 30s), rate_limit = 24%. Total error events in window (last 7d): 3,420.
Isha (Onboarding): is this affecting their onboarding flows or just background jobs?
Luca (CS Ops): mostly user-facing onboarding API calls — some auth handoffs and session init. Not background jobs mainly.
Marta (Customer Success Manager): Marta here — customer reported sign-up failures yesterday morning, escalation opened. Any targeted endpoints to share for the support ticket?
Luca (CS Ops): top failing endpoints (by error count):
```
1) POST /v1/accounts/onboard - 1,040 errs (30%) - 502 gateway timeouts
2) POST /v1/sessions/start - 760 errs (22%) - upstream 504/timeouts
3) GET /v1/models/list - 500 errs (15%) - rate_limited 429 from model-proxy
4) POST /v1/keys/validate - 420 errs (12%) - 502s during keyservice deploy window
5) POST /v1/chat/generate - 300 errs (9%) - intermittent 5xx when seq_len > 2048
6) Remaining endpoints - 400 errs (12%) - mixed client timeouts and 503s
```
Ava (CSE): thanks — that matches traces: sessions/start has a slow tail on p95. I can dig into traces and share a short trace link.
Luca (CS Ops): trace link: https://traces.redwood.example/r/abc123 (p95 ~1.9s, tail spikes to 6-10s during the window)
Isha (Onboarding): for onboarding impact: can we move /v1/accounts/onboard to the lower load slot or enable cached preflight? Any quick mitigations?
Luca (CS Ops): short mitigations proposed: 1) enable short-term prefix caching for model list requests, 2) add retry/backoff on sessions/start client with jitter, 3) temporarily route onboard traffic to Dedicated pool if they have capacity.
Marta (Customer Success Manager): customer prefers config changes rather than code changes. Routing to Dedicated is an ask they might accept. Can we estimate downtime/risk?
Luca (CS Ops): routing risk low, but requires provisioning — estimate 30-45m ops + config. Isha: can you ask customer if they can tolerate a scheduled 1h window?
Isha (Onboarding): pinged them, they said yes for a midnight window PST.
deploy-bot: [info] service/keyservice deployed at 2412345600 — saw increased error ratio during 2412345600-2412345660
Ava (CSE): that aligns — keyservice deploy correlates with spikes on /v1/keys/validate and some 502s. Suggest rolling back that deploy for deeper rollback-driven debug?
Luca (CS Ops): rollbacks are heavy — propose: revert the specific change causing longer auth validation path (from the deploy notes) or patch timeout threshold. I'll open a runbook step.
Marta (Customer Success Manager): I'll tell the customer the plan: 1) schedule midnight routing to Dedicated, 2) apply caching & client retry suggestions, 3) we are investigating deploy-caused 502s.
Ava (CSE): I'll attach a short query for engineers: Top offending trace IDs + example request bodies.
Luca (CS Ops): next actions: 
- Ava: post trace snippets by EOD (2412345720)
- Isha: confirm scheduled midnight window with customer (done)
- Ops (Luca): prepare Dedicated routing config and dry-run (ETA 30m)
- Marta: update customer's ticket with the above plan and set expectation for a follow-up after routing test.
Isha (Onboarding): noted, will update them.
Marta (Customer Success Manager): thanks team. Will mark this as high priority for renewal risk if not improved by next check-in. :warning:
Ava (CSE): one more note — /v1/chat/generate 5xxs spike when seq_len > 2048, suggest a soft limit check client-side until model quant/policy fix.
Luca (CS Ops): good call. I'll add a header-based guard for now.
Marta (Customer Success Manager): closing thread for now, will reopen if errors don't drop after mitigation window. :thumbsup:
